4. Payment of compound

SCHEDULE
- FORM 1
- FORM 2

LAWS OF MALAYSIA

MONEYLENDERS ACT 1951

MONEYLENDERS (COMPOUNDING OF OFFENCES)
REGULATIONS 2003

IN exercise of the powers conferred by section 29 H of the
Moneylenders Act 1951 [ Act 400], the Minister makes the following
regulations:

Citation and commencement

1. (1) These regulations may be cited as the Moneylenders
(Compounding of Offences) Regulations 2003.

 (2)  These Regulations come into operation on 1 November 2003.

Compoundable offences

2. The following offences may be compounded by the Registrar or
any officer authorized in writing by the Registrar:

(a) offences under subsections 5F(2), 9 E(3), 9 F(2), 9 G(4),
11(2), 16(2), 18(2), 19(4) and 25(1) of the Act; and

(b) offences under subregulations 3(2), 5(4), 6(4 ), 6(10) and
regulation 16 of the Moneylenders (Control and Licensing)
Regulations 2003 [P.U. (A) 400/2003].

6  Laws of Malaysia  P.U. (A) 401/2003

Method of compounding

3. (1)  Upon receipt of information or complaint that a
compoundable offence has been committed, any of such persons
mentioned in regulation 2 may issue a notice of offer to compound the
offence in Form 1 as prescribed in the Schedule.

 (2) The offer to compound an offence is for a period of fourteen
days, and if full payment of the sum offered is made on or before the
expiry of fourteen days, no further proceedings shall be taken against
the person who committed such offence. Otherwise, prosecution will
be instituted without further notice.

 (3) A person who accepts an offer to compound a compoundable
offence shall accept the offer in Form 2 as prescribed in the Schedule.

Payment of compound

4. (1) When an offer to compound any offence is made and
accepted, payment may be made in cash or by money order, postal
order, cashier's order, banker's order or banker's draft made payable
to the Registrar of Moneylenders and crossed with the words "Account
Payee Only" or through an electronic fund transfer.

 (2) Payment of compound under subregulation (1), other than
payment made through an electronic fund transfer, shall be as follows:

(a) if the payment is made i n cash, such payment shall be
delivered personally to the Registrar or the person
authorized to make the offer to compound; and

(b) if the payment is made by money order, postal order,
cashier's order, bankers's order or banker's draft, such
payment shall be delivered personally to the Registrar or
the person authorized to make the offer to compound or
sent by post to the address specified in the notice of offer
to compound the offence in Form 1 as prescribed in the
Schedule.
  Moneylenders (Compounding of Offences)   7
 Regulations 2003

 (3) Every payment received shall be considered as money
belonging to the Registrar of Moneylenders and an official receipt shall
be issued for such payment to the person to whom the offer to
compound was made.
